places.name: Komodo Airport, Labuan Bajo
places.what_it_is: The race's arrival/start gateway (IATA LBJ): the only airport in West Manggarai and the busiest in the region.
places.why_it_matters: Defines crew, media and rider-repatriation logistics for the start; also the fallback exit for a scratched rider anywhere in the west half of the course.
places.history_culture: Grew rapidly with Labuan Bajo's dive- and Komodo-tourism boom; still small enough that flight schedules shift with the tourist season.

practical.sleep: full range of hotels in town
practical.best_time: dry season (Apr-Oct) has the most flight capacity; Jun-Aug is also the busiest and priciest window

facts.fact: As of mid-2026, 8 airlines fly to Labuan Bajo from about 10 airports worldwide, and 8 airlines fly out to about 12 airports; Wings Air, Super Air Jet, AirAsia and Batik Air operate most flights.

Domestic routes: Denpasar (Bali) is the busiest link at 4-6 flights/day (~1 hour), plus Jakarta (5 airlines: AirAsia, Batik Air, Citilink, Garuda, Super Air Jet) and Praya/Lombok; Wings Air also flies Labuan Bajo-Ende direct.

Kuala Lumpur is the longest-haul direct international route (~3h40m). Jetstar Asia ended its twice-weekly Singapore-Labuan Bajo service on 31 July 2025; Scoot announced a twice-weekly Singapore replacement targeted for launch between Oct 2025 and Mar 2026, subject to regulatory approval.

photo_subjects: arriving/departing propeller aircraft with hills behind

places.name: H. Hasan Aroeboesman Airport, Ende
places.what_it_is: Ende's airport (IATA ENE), ~2 km from town centre; the region's main air-evacuation point for central Flores.
places.why_it_matters: Nearest airport to the Kelimutu/Lio section (08) of the course; a realistic medevac and crew-change point roughly at race mid-distance.

practical.sleep: hotels in Ende (n-ende: full resupply, reliable water, hotel sleep)

facts.fact: Wings Air is effectively the only scheduled operator at Ende, flying to Kupang and Labuan Bajo; some sources also list TransNusa and occasional Bali (Denpasar) service via Kupang.

Wings Air suspended flights on the Maumere-Ende-Larantuka cluster of routes during periods of Lewotobi eruption activity, evidence that regional flight schedules are exposed to the same volcanic hazard as the course's section 10.

photo_subjects: Ende airport apron with Iya volcano backdrop

places.name: Frans Seda Airport, Maumere
places.what_it_is: Maumere's airport (IATA MOF), ~5 km from town; nearest scheduled-flight gateway to the Sikka end of the course.
places.why_it_matters: Logistics and medevac point for sections 09-10; likely rider/crew changeover point near the race's last quarter.

practical.hazards: flights on this route periodically suspended during active Lewotobi eruption phases

facts.fact: Wings Air and Nam Air are the scheduled operators; Nam Air and Wings Air both fly non-stop from Kupang, Wings Air also connects Labuan Bajo and Makassar.

photo_subjects: small turboprop on the Maumere apron

places.name: Gewayantana Airport, Larantuka
places.what_it_is: Larantuka's airport (IATA LKA), ~9-15 km from town in Tiwatobi village; the finish town's air gateway.
places.why_it_matters: Finish-line logistics: rider/crew departures, medevac for the eastern end of the course, closest airport to the Lewotobi hazard zone the route must skirt.

practical.hazards: same eruption-driven flight suspensions as Ende/Maumere

facts.fact: Search results confirmed Larantuka's cluster (Ende-Maumere-Larantuka) shares Wings Air service and the same eruption-driven suspensions, but did not surface Gewayantana-specific route detail beyond what is already in data/pois.geojson (verified via Wikipedia and an airport directory).

places.name: Turelelo-Soa Airport, Bajawa
places.what_it_is: The airfield serving Bajawa (IATA BJW), ~23.5 km north of town in Soa sub-district.
places.why_it_matters: A secondary medevac/crew option near the Ngada megalith section (05) if Ende or Labuan Bajo are too far.

facts.fact: Not independently re-searched this session; data/pois.geojson already lists this as verified (Wikipedia, two articles) with scheduled flights to Kupang and Ende. No new source added.

places.name: Labuan Bajo harbour and the Sape ferry
places.what_it_is: The town's main pier/Pelni terminal; also the ASDP ferry link west across the Sape Strait to Sape, Sumbawa (the classic overland Bali-Flores backpacker route).
places.why_it_matters: A crew/logistics alternative to flying gear or a bike box in from Bali/Sumbawa; also the working port behind the tourist-boat harbour.

facts.fact: This session's ferry search returned good detail on the Larantuka-side ASDP network but did not surface a current Labuan Bajo-Sape timetable; that route is well documented elsewhere (it is the standard Bali-Flores overland ferry) but is left unverified here rather than guessed at.

photo_subjects: Labuan Bajo harbour at sunset with Komodo tour boats

places.name: Aimere ferry port
places.what_it_is: South-coast port of Ngada Regency, ~1 hour from Bajawa; ASDP ferry to Waingapu (Sumba) and to Kupang.
places.why_it_matters: Ferry option for crew/gear movement near section 05/06 of the course; also the logical jump-off if an Ultra epilogue via Sumba were ever considered.

facts.fact: Already verified in data/nodes.geojson (n-aimere): ASDP ferry to Waingapu (Tue/Fri) and to Kupang. Not re-searched independently this session; this session's ferry search focused on the Larantuka side per the brief.

places.name: Larantuka port and inter-island ferries
places.what_it_is: The finish town's port: ASDP ferries across the narrow Larantuka Strait to Adonara and Solor, and onward multi-stop routes to Lewoleba (Lembata) and Kupang (West Timor).
places.why_it_matters: A ferry epilogue to Adonara/Lembata is explicitly floated in route-concept.md as one way to extend an Ultra variant; also the practical route for spectators/media/riders' onward travel after the finish, since there is no direct ferry to Labuan Bajo.
places.history_culture: Larantuka is the Portuguese-Catholic Semana Santa town; the strait crossing to Adonara/Solor has been a fixed feature of Flores Timur life for centuries.

facts.fact: KMP Ile Labalekan runs Kupang-Lewoleba-Adonara-Larantuka, departing Kupang's Bolok terminal at 10:00, reaching Lewoleba the next morning, then continuing to Adonara and Larantuka before returning to Kupang.
KMP Ile Mandiri runs a Baranusa-Lewoleba-Solor-Larantuka rotation (departs ~02:00), also serving Adonara on the same multi-day loop out toward Kalabahi (Alor).

There is no direct ferry from Larantuka to Labuan Bajo; a surface route goes via Kupang and takes roughly 2 days 17 hours including transfers, confirming that inter-town gear/crew logistics along the finish end of the course should default to flights, not ferries.

ASDP schedules on this coast are frequently disrupted: a search hit shows Kupang-Larantuka-Aimere sailings cancelled outright on at least one occasion, underscoring that published timetables should be treated as indicative, not guaranteed, for race planning.

photo_subjects: Larantuka waterfront with ferries and Ile Mandiri behind

places.name: Trans-Flores Highway
places.what_it_is: The single paved road spanning Flores end to end, used by the course only as short links between sections, never as the course itself.
places.why_it_matters: The road figure anchors the brochure's core comparison: the highway needs far more distance to cross the island than a straight line would suggest, which is the seed of the race's own claim to reach 1,200-1,400+ km off-highway.

practical.access: the island's one continuous paved corridor, Labuan Bajo-Ruteng-Bajawa-Ende-Moni-Maumere-Larantuka
practical.best_time: dry season (Apr-Oct); highland/rainy-season stretches (Nov-Mar) can be difficult
practical.hazards: slow, winding mountain road; rarely a flat or straight stretch over 100 m; some central-highland sections degrade in the rainy season

facts.fact: Sources differ on exact length: one guide gives ~500 km Labuan Bajo-Maumere by road versus ~250 km straight-line; another gives ~660 km of asphalt for a ~375 km direct distance end-to-end. Both describe the same phenomenon the concept doc cites (~670 km actual road length across the island) but the two figures are not identical, so the highway's precise length should be read as approximate, not a single settled number.

The road is mostly asphalt and generally in good condition, but average driving speed is only around 35 km/h because of continuous bends and mountainous terrain; central-highland stretches can be more difficult in the Nov-Mar wet season.

photo_subjects: roadside market stall on the highway

places.name: Labuan Bajo (resupply hub and start town)
places.what_it_is: Race start town: fully geared for international tourism, with the region's only hospital-grade private facility.
places.why_it_matters: The best-equipped town on the whole course; the natural place to stage bikes, spares and a pre-race medical check.
places.history_culture: Boomed from a fishing village into the Komodo dive/tour gateway over the last two decades.

practical.best_time: Jun-Aug busiest and priciest; Apr-May and Sep-Oct similar weather with fewer crowds

facts.fact: Siloam Hospitals Labuan Bajo, a 3-storey private hospital on Jl. Gabriel Gampur, is the only hospital facility in Labuan Bajo/West Manggarai Regency.

Labuan Bajo has many motorbike/scooter rental outlets (e.g. Bajo Rental) but the search did not find a dedicated pedal-bicycle shop; rental and repair infrastructure in town is built around motorbikes and dive/tour gear, not cycling.

Telkomsel is repeatedly cited as the most reliable operator for Flores/remote-island coverage (Opensignal's 2026 report gives it a Coverage Experience score of 8.6/10 nationally); Indosat/IM3 is a cheaper second choice that is solid in towns and tourist areas but weaker off the beaten track. SIM cards are easiest bought at airport kiosks.

places.name: Ruteng (resupply hub)
places.what_it_is: Cool highland town (1,168-1,188 m), Manggarai Regency capital; the best full resupply in the western region per data/nodes.geojson.
places.why_it_matters: First major resupply/medical point after leaving Labuan Bajo (end of sections 02-03).
places.history_culture: Catholic hill town; near the Cancar lingko spider-web rice fields.

facts.fact: Ruteng has a general regional hospital (RSUD Ruteng) in Watu, Langke Rembong district.

places.name: Bajawa (resupply hub)
places.what_it_is: Cool highland Ngada Regency capital on the Trans-Flores highway near the megalithic villages.
places.why_it_matters: Main resupply and medical point for the section 05 cultural checkpoints (Bena, Luba, Tololela, Gurusina).
places.history_culture: Gateway to the Ngada megalithic villages under Inerie volcano.

facts.fact: Bajawa has a general regional hospital on Jl. Diponegoro, Trikora.

photo_subjects: Bajawa hillside town with Inerie volcano behind

places.name: Ende (resupply hub)
places.what_it_is: Largest town of central Flores, Ende Regency capital, on the south coast under Iya volcano.
places.why_it_matters: Full resupply and medical point roughly at the course's midpoint, gateway to the signature Kelimutu section.
places.history_culture: Sukarno's 1934-38 exile town, said to have conceived the Pancasila under a breadfruit tree there.

practical.access: on Trans-Flores highway, coastal, airport ~2 km

facts.fact: Ende General Hospital (RSUD) is on Jl. Prof. Dr. W.Z. Yohanes.

A Tripadvisor forum thread discusses renting a (motor)bike from Ende toward Labuan Bajo, evidence that one-way rental/logistics between Ende and the west is an established, if informal, practice -- but no dedicated cycle shop was found.

places.name: Maumere (resupply hub)
places.what_it_is: Sikka Regency capital, largest town of eastern Flores; rebuilt after the 1992 earthquake/tsunami.
places.why_it_matters: Last major full-resupply/medical town before the Egon-Lewotobi-Larantuka finish stretch (sections 09-10).
places.history_culture: Devastated by the 12 Dec 1992 earthquake and tsunami; rebuilt since.

practical.access: on Trans-Flores highway, coastal, airport ~5 km
practical.hazards: earthquake/tsunami history; Lewotobi corridor further east

facts.fact: Regional General Hospital Dr. TC Hillers is on Jl. Wairklau, Kota Uneng, Alok district, Maumere.
Maumere has one larger rental/repair station serving overland motorbike travellers -- more limited than Labuan Bajo's cluster -- and again no dedicated pedal-cycle shop surfaced in search.

places.name: Larantuka (resupply hub, hospital)
places.what_it_is: Race finish town, Flores Timur Regency capital, under Ile Mandiri.
places.history_culture: Semana Santa Holy Week procession tradition, continuous since the 16th century.

practical.access: on Trans-Flores highway, coastal, airport 9-15 km, port
practical.hazards: Lewotobi volcanic activity to the west, on the approach

facts.fact: RSUD Larantuka is on Jl. Sudirman, Larantuka.

photo_subjects: Semana Santa procession imagery (if licensing permits)

places.name: Komodo National Park gateway
places.what_it_is: The marine/national park surrounding Labuan Bajo, gateway attraction for the race's start town; not itself on the course but shapes the town's tourist economy, pricing and crowding.
places.why_it_matters: Explains why Labuan Bajo is expensive and crowded in peak months, and gives the brochure a hook on entry-fee/visitor-cap changes that also affect general Indonesia travel costs riders and crew will face.
places.history_culture: UNESCO World Heritage site for komodo dragons and marine biodiversity.

practical.fees_protocol: pre-booking increasingly required in high season
practical.best_time: Jul-Oct is described as the busiest, most booked-out window

facts.fact: Sources give differing 2026 entrance-fee figures -- one cites a park entrance fee of IDR 650,000 per person, another an IDR 250,000/person/day marine park fee (~USD 15) -- indicating the fee structure has multiple components (entrance, marine park, activity- and boat-specific charges) rather than one flat number; treat any single figure quoted in the brochure as indicative and to be reconfirmed close to race date.
Reported plan: from 1 April 2026 the park operates under a 1,000-visitor-per-day quota with mandatory pre-booking; slots in the July-October high season are said to book out 3-6 months ahead.

Indonesia's Visa on Arrival / e-VOA is currently listed at IDR 500,000 (~USD 35) for 30 days, but a proposed 2026 increase would raise it to roughly USD 42 (e-VOA) or USD 56 (airport VOA) -- not yet confirmed as final at time of writing, so brochure copy should say 'check current fee before travel' rather than quote one number as settled.

Labuan Bajo/Komodo's dry season runs roughly April-October; June-August is consistently described as the busiest and highest-priced window, with April-May and September-October offering similar weather with fewer crowds and better rates.

places.name: Silk Road Mountain Race (reference format)
places.what_it_is: The Kyrgyzstan ultra-distance bikepacking race the Flores race deliberately borrows its format from: single stage, fixed route, self-supported, staffed checkpoints, generous time limit.
places.why_it_matters: Gives the brochure a credible, existing benchmark for what kind of event this is and roughly how big a field and how hard a course to expect, without inventing Flores-specific numbers before scouting is done.
places.history_culture: Founded by Nelson Trees; one of the originating races of the modern self-supported ultra-distance bikepacking-race genre alongside the Tour Divide/Trans Am lineage; the organisers also run the Atlas and Hellenic Mountain Races on the same model.

practical.fees_protocol: entirely self-supported: no third-party support or private resupply; riders carry or buy everything from commercially available services along the route

facts.fact: Distance and climbing vary by year: recent editions are cited around 1,900 km / 30,000 m of climbing, and the 2026 edition specifically at about 2,052 km with roughly 35,362 m of elevation gain.
Riders are given a time limit commonly described as 14 days, with most finishers taking roughly 8-14 days.
The race is fully self-supported (no 3rd-party or private resupply) and requires riders to pass through staffed checkpoints named in the race manual; recent editions have run 3 staffed checkpoints.
Field size has varied by year; the 2019 edition is cited as having 135 riders start.

photo_subjects: No Flores-specific imagery -- if used in the brochure, credit as a reference-format callout rather than a Flores photo

narrative_notes: The brochure's honest hook is the contrast between a thin, well-serviced spine (five small airports, a paved highway, hospitals and full resupply in six towns) and how quickly that infrastructure thins once the route leaves it: no dedicated bike shops were found anywhere on the island (only motorbike/scooter rental and repair), ferry schedules on the eastern side are explicitly unreliable/cancellable, and the Lewotobi eruption has already interrupted scheduled flights on the Ende-Maumere-Larantuka cluster -- the same corridor the course's most dangerous section must skirt. Visa and Komodo NP fees are both in flux for 2026 (proposed increases, new quota/pre-booking rules); the brochure should quote current, checkable figures rather than freeze a number that may already be stale by race week. Homestay pricing and culture, and Labuan Bajo's exact busiest-month ranking, were not independently confirmed this session (search budget spent on higher-priority items); route-concept.md's own claim that August is the safest weather bet but also the busiest month is consistent with what was found (Jun-Aug busiest) but not verified with a dedicated search.
corrections_to_data: None required. All existing data/pois.geojson and data/nodes.geojson entries checked against search results were consistent (Ende, Maumere, Larantuka, Bajawa/Soa airports; Aimere ferry; town resupply/water/sleep tiers). No coordinate or classification errors found.
open_questions: Labuan Bajo-Sape ferry: current ASDP schedule/frequency not found this session; needs a dedicated search or a direct ASDP source.

Homestay typical nightly price and booking culture on Flores (outside Labuan Bajo hotels) -- not searched; floreshomestay.org and floressustainabletravel.blog surfaced as leads worth reading directly.

No dedicated bicycle shop (as opposed to motorbike rental) was found in Labuan Bajo, Ende or Maumere -- confirm with a scouting-team ground check whether any exists, since the concept doc's own POI notes call Maumere's resupply 'bike-ish parts' only.

Both the Indonesia visa-on-arrival fee increase and the Komodo NP fee/quota changes for 2026 were described in sources as proposed or recently changed -- reconfirm both against official government/park sources close to race date rather than trusting any figure in this file as final.

Trans-Flores highway total length has two materially different figures in the sources found (~500 km vs ~660 km of asphalt); reconcile against the route-concept.md figure (~670 km) with an official source if the brochure needs one precise number.
